name: ProDy
summary: Protein structural dynamics, elastic-network modes and comparative structure analysis.

steps: The reviewed conda-forge ProDy 2.6.1 release has Linux/macOS x86_64 packages but no native Windows build. Do not run this conda recipe in native Windows.
If needed, prepare a separate WSL2 Linux environment and rerun plan there, or review the maintainer's Windows installation instructions and compatible packages manually.
manual_fallback.verify_note: In the chosen Linux environment, import ProDy and run the small local mode-analysis check. Do not treat a native Windows install as verified by this recipe.

argv: import numpy as np, prody; g=prody.GNM('synthetic'); g.buildKirchhoff(np.array([[0.,0.,0.],[1.,0.,0.],[0.,1.,0.],[0.,0.,1.]])); g.calcModes(n_modes=1); assert g.numModes()==1; print(prody.__version__)

notes: This route runs a tiny local Gaussian network model on synthetic coordinates to check core functionality. It is not molecular-dynamics simulation or validation of biological dynamics. Optional database access, GUI plugins and external applications are outside this installation.
The pinned conda-forge release has Linux/macOS x86_64 artifacts only. Architecture and solver compatibility must be checked again on the user's machine.
